unit: ft NAVD88, max 5 ft 4 in NAVD88 (conformance tolerance)
qualifier: Lighthouse Point sets its own rule: seawall caps must be at least 4.0 ft NAVD88 (5.5 ft NGVD29), and owners may raise them to 5.0 ft NAVD88. A new or substantially rebuilt seawall must be designed so the cap can be built to 5.0 ft NAVD88. Because of settling, a cap between 3 ft 8 in and 5 ft 4 in NAVD88 counts as compliant.
detail_rows: Minimum cap :: no less than 4.0 ft NAVD88 (5.5 ft NGVD29) - LDC Sec. 33-18(a), Ord. 2024-1033 (re-enacting Ord. 2023-0998) | Allowed raise :: owners authorized to raise or cap to 5.0 ft NAVD88 (6.5 ft NGVD29) - Sec. 33-18(a) | Tolerance :: 3 ft 8 in to 5 ft 4 in NAVD88 (5 ft 2 in to 6 ft 10 in NGVD29) considered in conformance - Sec. 33-18(a) | New or substantial rehab :: must be designed to accommodate a cap built to 5.0 ft NAVD88 - Sec. 33-18(a)(1) | Return walls :: required where the new wall is higher than the neighbouring property - Sec. 33-18(a)(2) | Existing low walls :: walls below 3 ft 8 in NAVD88 may remain until 50% or more is repaired/reconstructed or the lot is redeveloped - Sec. 33-18(b) | Retaining wall behind seawall :: max 3 ft high or 6 ft NAVD88 at the cap, whichever is less - Sec. 33-18(d)
source: City of Lighthouse Point Land Development Code Ch. 33 (Shoreline Development) Sec. 33-18, adopted by Ord. No. 2024-1033; amendment originally Ord. No. 2023-0998 (former Sec. 42-381)
notes: The online Municode code for Lighthouse Point is stale (Supp. 21, 2018) and still shows old Sec. 42-381 with 4.0 ft NAVD88 and a 4 ft 4 in NAVD88 max. The current rule comes from adopted but uncodified ordinances on the city's MuniDocs page: Ord. 2023-0998 (raised the authorized height to 5.0 and the tolerance max to 5 ft 4 in) and Ord. 2024-1033 Exhibit A 'Final version to be codified' Sec. 33-18. Text was read from a scanned PDF via OCR. Exhibit B of 2024-1033 has handwritten edits that seem to add 2035/2050 phase-in wording and strike the tolerance, which doesn't match the clean Exhibit A; the OCR couldn't resolve this, so a person should read the PDF. Second-reading date (2024) is not legible in the OCR. Ord. 2023-0998 is also in OrdBank: https://library.municode.com/fl/lighthouse_point/ordinances/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=1310337. Not checked: whether Broward Co. Code Sec. 39-407 applies inside the city.

unit: ft NAVD88, max BFE (7.0 if BFE is 5.0)
qualifier: New seawalls in Hillsboro Beach must have a top elevation of at least 5.0 ft NAVD88. The top generally may not be higher than the property's FEMA base flood elevation; where the BFE is 5.0 ft the maximum is 7.0 ft NAVD88. Walls must also be designed so they can be raised at least 24 inches later.
detail_rows: Minimum :: 5.0 ft NAVD88 for newly constructed seawalls - Code Sec. 12-268(D) | Max (BFE of 5.0 or more) :: the property's base flood elevation - Sec. 12-268(D) table | Max (BFE equal to 5.0) :: 7.0 ft NAVD88 - Sec. 12-268(D) | Max (X zone) :: per the code's definition of grade (BFE for lowest floor on the FIRM) - Sec. 12-268(D) | Waiver :: Town Commission may allow lower walls where the habitable finished floor is below 5.0 ft NAVD88 - Sec. 12-268(D) | Future raising :: must be designed to be raised at least 24 in - Sec. 12-268(D)(6) | Docks :: fixed docks max 10 in above the adjacent seawall - Sec. 12-268(D)(2)
source: Hillsboro Beach Code of Ordinances Ch. 12 (LDC), Art. XIII, Sec. 12-268 (Ords. 2017-294, 2020-05, 2021-05)
notes: Town has its own rule with no 4.0 ft interim; it also says substantially repaired walls must perform as tidal flood barriers by 1 Jan 2035 at 5.0 ft NAVD88. The code's table rows look internally inconsistent ('greater than or equal to 5.0' -> max BFE, then 'equal to 5.0' -> max 7.0); reproduced as written. Municode Supp. 16.
